purpose: Authoritative-vendor review adding Evocon OEE / Production Monitoring as a manufacturing production-intelligence source at spec-verified. Current provider documentation confirms a cloud reporting API using API-key/secret Basic Authentication, a dedicated Custom reports right that is read-only for /api/reports/... but covers all stations, and an alternative User rights mode that can inherit read-write authority for selected stations and support production-order automation. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, device API access or plant-network access were used.

systems.name: Evocon OEE / Production Monitoring
systems.evidenceNote: Provider-owned Evocon support documentation confirms API-key/secret Basic Authentication. A Custom reports key grants read-only access to api.evocon.com/api/reports/... and all stations; User rights can instead copy an existing user's rights, including read-write access for selected stations, and is intended for integrations such as sending production orders. Product documentation establishes factories/stations/shifts, production quantities and targets, production speed, downtime/speed-loss/quality loss context, stop reasons and production-order workflows, but the exact public reporting endpoint schema, pagination and rate limits were not exposed in the unauthenticated documentation reviewed. No authenticated calls were made.
securityEvidenceBlockers: The documented Custom reports credential is read-only but covers all stations. Before authentication evidence advances, the customer must explicitly approve that company-wide station scope or provide a customer-controlled read projection/export that narrows data without granting write authority.

Do not substitute a User rights API key merely to obtain narrower station scope: provider documentation states that User rights can inherit read-write authority and support production-order automation. Prove an effectively read-only rights set if that route is ever used.

requiredPermissions: prefer the documented Custom reports API key for steady-state WFM reads because it is explicitly read-only
obtain explicit customer approval for its all-stations visibility; do not silently expand from a requested subset to company-wide data
pin api.evocon.com and the /api/reports/... namespace; do not follow undocumented hosts or cross-host redirects
do not use a User rights key unless an authorised environment proves its effective operations are read-only for the required stations
store API key/secret only in the executor credential boundary; never place Basic Authorization values, API keys or secrets in evidence/catalogue/log payloads
prove credential rotation/revocation and company binding before advancing authentication evidence
dataAvailableOrExpected: reporting API production data for external analytics; exact endpoint schemas require authorised proof
factory/station and shift performance context from the Evocon production model
production quantities, production speed and target-versus-actual performance context
OEE and component/loss context including downtime, speed loss and quality loss
planned/unplanned stop context and operator-classified stop reasons
product and production-order context where configured; vendor material confirms production-order automation exists but normal WFM runtime writes remain disabled
quality/maintenance/checklist context exists in the product model; exact reporting API exposure must be proven before mapping as authoritative fields
operator/lead-operator references may exist in product workflows; do not treat them as employment or payroll authority
stableIdentifiers: Exact factory/station/product/order/report identifiers are not sufficiently established in the unauthenticated public API material reviewed; authenticated schema proof must capture provider IDs and reject display-name-only mappings.

freshnessLatency.application: Evocon markets real-time shift/factory production monitoring, but application freshness must not be assumed to equal reporting-API freshness
freshnessLatency.reportingApi: public documentation confirms reporting extraction but does not state endpoint-specific latency or change-watermark semantics; preserve source/report period plus ingestion time until proven
freshnessLatency.outageRecovery: provider status history shows delayed processing can later recover data, so late-arriving records must reconcile historical windows rather than masquerade as current events

paginationDeltaEvents.pagination: not publicly established for the reporting endpoints reviewed; authenticated proof must discover bounded paging/row limits before large backfills
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: not publicly established; first implementation should use bounded time windows plus overlapping reconciliation until a vendor-supported change watermark is proven
paginationDeltaEvents.webhooks: no trusted reporting webhook contract established by the reviewed API documentation; scheduled authenticated reads remain the default completeness path

rateLimitsAndRetries: numeric reporting-API rate limits were not established in the reviewed public documentation; respect any provider response headers and fail closed rather than inventing quotas
use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for retryable HTTP/network failures
Basic-auth credentials are long-lived static authority, so repeated 401/403 responses must stop automatic retries and enter credential diagnostics rather than brute-force looping
large historical pulls must use bounded windows/checkpoints and reconcile counts/totals to avoid silent gaps if pagination semantics are later discovered
versionsRegionsCustomFields: current public material documents api.evocon.com; no regional API hosts or public version-negotiation contract were established
Evocon is documented as a cloud-based service used across factories/countries; preserve each factory/station's local timezone and shift calendar when normalising production periods
stop-reason taxonomies and operational classifications are customer-configurable; map by provider IDs when available and preserve local labels as extensions rather than globally equating text labels
unit/quantity semantics can vary by product and station; normalisation must retain source unit, canonical unit, conversion rule and confidence
do not assume product UI fields are exposed by every reporting endpoint
automationOpportunities: compare real production progress, target speed and remaining demand with scheduled labour to forecast likely overtime before shift end
redeploy qualified available workers between lines when output loss or downtime creates a material staffing imbalance, subject to Product Evolution decision policy
combine downtime/stop reasons with maintenance skills and availability to coordinate response labour and reduce avoidable downtime
join good output and payable labour cost to calculate labour cost per good unit and identify lines/shifts where labour spend is not converting into throughput
join quality-loss/reject context with labour time to expose rework labour burden and target training/process interventions
use production-order progress as a demand signal for agency/overtime planning without making Evocon the payroll or contract authority

join production output with an authoritative energy meter/tariff source to calculate energy per good unit and cost per unit; Evocon production output supplies the denominator, not authoritative energy consumption
reconcile Evocon station/factory structures to ERP/MES/WFM site and work-centre identities once stable provider IDs are proven
savingsHypotheses: reduce overtime and agency use by detecting during-shift production shortfall early enough to redeploy qualified internal labour instead of reacting at shift end
reduce paid idle time and downtime by aligning stop/downtime reasons with available maintenance and operations capability
improve product and order costing by joining Evocon actual output/run-loss context with WFM payable labour cost and ERP finance dimensions
reduce rework labour by correlating quality-loss patterns with staffing, skill mix and intervention history
improve energy cost per good unit by combining Evocon good-output denominator with separately authoritative energy/tariff data
speed implementation for manufacturers already using Evocon because the connector reuses the existing HTTPS REST fabric and does not require direct plant/device access
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve recommendation timestamp, chosen action, action effective time, production baseline window and post-action outcome window
retain competing changes such as maintenance action, material change, product/changeover and planned stop so labour interventions are not falsely credited for correlated OEE movement
preserve source/report period, ingestion time and late-recovery status for backfilled production data
dataGaps: public reporting documentation reviewed does not enumerate endpoint schemas, stable IDs, pagination, delta/change tokens, numeric rate limits or API version negotiation
application UI is real-time, but reporting API latency and completeness guarantees are not publicly established
Custom reports is least-write-risk but broadest read scope because it covers all stations; customer-approved scope evidence is required
User rights can be station-scoped but may be read-write, creating a least-privilege trade-off that cannot be resolved by assuming narrower scope is safer
Evocon is not authoritative for employment contracts, leave entitlement, payable time, payroll rules, worker qualifications, agency commercials, energy meter readings or finance ledger truth
operator references, stop reasons and checklist classifications can be customer-defined and require identity/schema mapping before cross-site comparison
constraintsRisks: API key and secret are long-lived static credentials delivered through Basic Authentication; rotation, revocation, secure injection and accidental evidence/log leakage must be controlled
Custom reports keys expose all stations, so a small WFM use case requesting one line must not silently ingest the whole company
User rights credentials may permit production-order writes or other automation; successful authentication is not evidence of read-only authority
reporting API may have endpoint-specific limits/large-result behavior that is not yet publicly documented
factory/country/shift comparisons can be wrong if local timezone, DST, planned-stop conventions or customer-specific stop taxonomies are flattened
historical service incidents show source processing can be delayed and later recovered, so freshness diagnostics and replay reconciliation are required
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain an authorised Evocon Professional/Enterprise trial or customer-approved test account. Create a Custom reports key, explicitly approve or constrain its all-stations scope, prove api.evocon.com host/company binding, denied mutation paths, secret rotation/revocation, representative report schemas/stable IDs, timezone/unit semantics, backfill/pagination behavior and reconciliation after delayed/duplicate/partial reads. If the customer requires station-scoped access, prove a User rights identity whose effective operations are read-only before allowing it; never trade narrower resource scope for write-capable authority. Keep device APIs and production-order writes outside the WFM runtime authority.
